concepts.title: Forces Shaping the Earth's Surface
concepts.definition: The earth's surface is constantly shaped by two families of forces: internal forces from within the earth that raise mountains and trigger earthquakes and volcanoes, and external forces of weathering and erosion that wear the relief down and redeposit it.
concepts.key_idea: Building forces within, wearing forces without: the landscape is their tug-of-war.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest102.txt opening sections (what shapes the earth's surface)
question_patterns: what forces shape the earth's surface
differentiate internal and external forces with examples
which forces wear down the landforms
explain how the same force builds and destroys landforms

solution_steps.explain: Movements inside the earth fold, fault and lift the crust.
Weathering and erosion wear and redeposit the surface.
Present landforms record the balance of both force families.

concepts.title: Weathering and Erosion
concepts.definition: Weathering breaks rocks in place through sun, water, frost and living things; erosion carries the broken material away through rivers, wind, glaciers and sea waves, depositing it as plains, deltas and sand dunes elsewhere.
concepts.key_idea: Weathering breaks, erosion carries, deposition builds - the three-step landform cycle.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest102.txt sections on weathering, erosion and deposition
question_patterns: differentiate weathering and erosion with examples
how do rivers shape the land - describe the landforms
what landforms does wind create in deserts
how do glaciers change the surface of the earth
name the agents of erosion and their work
explain deposition with two landform examples

solution_steps.explain: Weathering crumbles rock without moving it far.
Rivers, wind, waves and glaciers transport the debris.
Deposition lays down plains, deltas and dunes.

concepts.title: Landforms and Human Life
concepts.definition: Mountains, plateaus and plains each host distinct human activities - farming in plains, herding and tourism in mountains, mining on plateaus - while hazards like earthquakes demand that settlements respect the forces shaping the land.
concepts.key_idea: Landform decides livelihood: plains farm, mountains herd, plateaus mine.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest102.txt sections on landforms and human adaptation
question_patterns: compare life in mountains, plateaus and plains
why are plains densely populated - give reasons
what economic activities suit a plateau region
how should people prepare for earthquake hazards
how has a landform shaped the life of people in your region
relate landforms to transport and settlement patterns

solution_steps.explain: Relief, soil and climate set the possibilities.
Farming, herding, mining or trade follow the land.
Preparedness for quakes and floods completes wise settlement.
